title: Wonders Grade 4 – Lesson 15: Your World Up Close

essential.d: very important; you must have it

question.d: something you ask to find out the answer
question.ex: The boy put up his hand to ask a question.

read.d: to look at words and understand them
read.ex: I read a book before bed.

learn.d: to get to know something new
learn.ex: I learn to ride a bike.

look.d: to use your eyes to see something
look.ex: Look at the bird in the tree!

picture.ex: I drew a picture of my cat.

use.d: to do something with a thing
use.ex: I use a spoon to eat soup.

make.d: to build something or to do something new
make.ex: Mom and I make a cake.

help.d: to make something easier for someone
help.ex: I help my mom carry the bags.

water.d: what is in rivers, seas and rain; we drink it
water.ex: I drink water after I play.

part.d: one piece of a whole thing
part.ex: A wheel is a part of a bike.

world.d: the Earth and everything on it; also, all the things around you
world.ex: I want to travel around the world one day.

up_close.d: from very near, so you can see small things
up_close.ex: At the zoo, we saw a giraffe up close.

close.d: near; not far away. Closer = more near
close.ex: Sit closer to me so you can see the book.

discover.d: to find or learn something for the first time
discover.ex: We discovered a bird’s nest in the tree.

closely.d: carefully, looking at every small part
closely.ex: Look closely at the ladybug on the leaf.

tool.d: a thing you hold and use to do a job
tool.ex: Dad uses a tool to fix my bike.

allow.ex: Mom allows me to play outside after my homework.

see.d: to use your eyes to know what is there
see.ex: I can see the moon tonight.

everyday.d: normal; used or seen every day
everyday.ex: A spoon, a cup and a toothbrush are everyday objects.

object.d: a thing you can see and touch
object.ex: There are many objects on my desk.

compare.d: to look at two things to see how they are the same or different
compare.ex: Compare the two apples. Which one is bigger?

gritty.d: rough, with very small hard pieces in it, like sand
gritty.ex: My hands are gritty after I play in the sand.

grain.d: a very small, hard piece of something, like sand, salt or sugar
grain.ex: There is a grain of sand on my finger.

sugar.d: small white pieces that make food and drinks sweet
sugar.ex: I put a little sugar on my strawberries.

crystal.d: a small hard piece with flat sides and sharp edges; salt and sugar are made of crystals
crystal.ex: With a magnifying glass, I can see that salt is made of tiny crystals.

left.d: the side that is opposite to right
left.ex: The cup is on the left, and the book is on the right.

diamond.d: a very hard, clear stone that shines
diamond.ex: Grandma’s ring has a small diamond.

glass.d: a hard, clear thing that you can see through; windows are made of it
glass.ex: The window is made of glass.

prism.d: a clear piece of glass with flat sides; light that goes through it can split into rainbow colors
prism.ex: White light goes into the prism, and a rainbow comes out.

step_back.d: to move your foot back, away from something
step_back.ex: Please take a step back from the edge of the pool.

too.d: more than is good or OK
too.ex: This soup is too hot to eat.

extreme.d: very, very great or strong; much more than usual
extreme.ex: The North Pole has extreme cold.

close_up.d: a photo taken very near something, so it looks big
close_up.ex: I took a close-up of a flower with my phone.

electron_microscope.d: a very big and strong microscope; it can make things look thousands or even millions of times bigger, and it shows the picture on a computer
electron_microscope.ex: The scientist uses an electron microscope to see a fly’s eye.

microscope.d: a tool that makes very small things look much bigger
microscope.ex: I look at a leaf with a microscope.

magnify.d: to make something look bigger than it really is. Magnified = made to look bigger
magnify.ex: A magnifying glass can magnify the lines on a leaf.

item.d: one thing, often one thing in a list or group
item.ex: I have three items in my basket: an apple, milk and bread.

thousand.d: many, many; more than two thousand (1,000 = one thousand)
thousand.ex: There are thousands of stars in the sky.

times.d: used to say how much bigger or how many more. 3 times bigger = as big as 3 of them
times.ex: An elephant is many times bigger than a dog.

actual.ex: In the book, the ladybug looks big, but its actual size is very small.

size.d: how big or small something is
size.ex: These shoes are the wrong size. They are too small.

high_tech.d: using the newest machines and computers
high_tech.ex: Our school has a high-tech robot.

take.d: to make a photo with a camera
take.ex: Dad took a picture of me at the park.

look_seem.d: to seem; to be like this when you see it

call.d: to give a name to someone or something

photomicrograph.d: a photo of something taken through a microscope
photomicrograph.ex: This photomicrograph shows the tiny parts of an onion skin.

huge.ex: The whale is huge next to the small boat.

word.d: a sound or group of letters that has a meaning
word.ex: My baby brother can say his first word.

micro.d: a word part that means very small (microscope = a tool to see very small things)
micro.ex: Micro means small, so a microscope helps us see small things, like tiny germs.

mean.d: to have as its idea; to say the same as another word

small.ex: The kitten is small, and the dog is big.

photomicrography.ex: In photomicrography, a camera is put on top of a microscope.

date_back.d: to start or be made at a time long ago
date_back.ex: This old teapot dates back to when Grandma was a little girl.

scientist.d: a person who studies how the world works
scientist.ex: The scientist looks at a plant in her lab.

named.ex: I have a cat named Coco.

donne.d: a French doctor and scientist. In 1840 he took some of the first photos through a microscope
donne.ex: Alfred Donné took photos of tiny things through a microscope.

first.d: before all the others; number one
first.ex: I was the first one to finish the race!

photograph.d: a photo; to photograph = to take a photo
photograph.ex: We photographed the ducks at the lake.

image.ex: The image on the screen is very clear.

around.d: about; a little more or a little less than
around.ex: There are around twenty children in my class.

german.d: from Germany, a country in Europe
german.ex: My friend Hans is German. He was born in Germany.

pharmacist.d: a person who gets medicine ready and sells it in a drugstore
pharmacist.ex: The pharmacist gives my mom the medicine.

version.d: one form of something that is a little different from the others
version.ex: My new bike is a better version of my old one.

camera.ex: I take photos with my camera.

bentley.d: a farmer in Vermont, USA. He took the first photos of snowflakes through a microscope, so people called him “Snowflake”
bentley.ex: Wilson Bentley took photos of more than 5,000 snowflakes.

vermont.d: a state in the north-east of the USA, with green mountains and cold, snowy winters
vermont.ex: In winter, Vermont gets a lot of snow.

person.d: a man, a woman or a child
person.ex: There is one person on the bench.

built_in.d: made as part of something, not a separate thing
built_in.ex: My phone has a built-in camera.

snowflake.d: one small piece of snow; it has six sides or six arms
snowflake.ex: A snowflake landed on my black glove.

typical.d: normal; like most others of its kind
typical.ex: On a typical school day, I walk to school with my mom.

thing.d: an object; something you can see or touch
thing.ex: Put your things in your bag.

unique.d: the only one like it; different from all others
unique.ex: My drawing is unique. Nobody has one like it.

nowadays.d: now; these days (not in the past)
nowadays.ex: Nowadays, many people read books on tablets.

micrograph.d: a picture taken through a microscope; an electron micrograph is made with an electron microscope
micrograph.ex: The electron micrograph shows the tiny hairs on a fly’s leg.

shaped.ex: This cookie is shaped like a star.

hexagon.d: a flat shape with six sides
hexagon.ex: Each little room in a honeycomb is a hexagon.

light_microscope.d: a microscope that uses light to show small things; we use this kind in school
light_microscope.ex: We look at onion skin with a light microscope in class.

school.d: a place where children go to learn
school.ex: I walk to school every day.

weak.ex: My old flashlight is weak. Its light is not bright.

detail.d: a small part or fact that you see when you look carefully
detail.ex: Look at all the details on the butterfly’s wings.

powerful.ex: This powerful truck can pull a big bus.

eye.d: the part of your face that you see with
eye.ex: I close my eyes when I sleep.

own.d: belonging to you, not to someone else

skin.d: the outside cover of a body
skin.ex: I put sun cream on my skin at the beach.

cell.d: one of the very, very small parts that all living things are made of; we need a microscope to see cells
cell.ex: We saw onion skin cells under the microscope.

dust_mite.d: a very, very tiny animal that lives in dust in our homes; it has eight legs and we need a microscope to see it
dust_mite.ex: Dust mites live in beds and carpets.

below.ex: The cat sleeps below the table.

human.ex: A human hand has five fingers.

capture.d: to catch; to keep a picture of something
capture.ex: My camera captured my dog in the air!

magnification.d: how much bigger something looks under a microscope or magnifying glass
magnification.ex: With more magnification, a hair looks like a big tree trunk.

million.d: the number 1,000,000; a very, very big number
million.ex: Millions of people live in my city.

original.d: the first one, before any copies or changes
original.ex: This is the original painting. The others are copies.

cause.ex: Germs can cause a cold, so wash your hands!

disease.d: something that makes people, animals or plants sick

year.ex: There are four seasons in a year.

behave.d: to act in a certain way
behave.ex: The children behave well in class.

inside.ex: The cat is inside the box.

dissolve.d: to mix into a liquid and seem to go away

drop.d: a very small round bit of a liquid
drop.ex: A drop of rain fell on my nose.

fingerprint.d: the pattern of thin lines on the end of your finger
fingerprint.ex: I left a fingerprint on the window.

mold.d: a soft, fuzzy green, white or blue thing that grows on old food
mold.ex: There is mold on this old bread. Don’t eat it!

strawberry.d: a small, sweet red fruit with tiny seeds on the outside

grape.d: a small round fruit; grapes grow in bunches
grape.ex: I eat purple grapes for a snack.

change.d: to become different; a change = when something becomes different
change.ex: The leaves change color in the fall.

over_time.d: slowly, as days, weeks or years go by
over_time.ex: Over time, the little tree grew very tall.

for_example.d: here is one thing that shows what I mean
for_example.ex: I like fruit, for example apples and bananas.

piece.ex: Can I have a piece of cake?

fruit.d: the sweet part of a plant that you can eat, like an apple or an orange

decay.d: to go bad and slowly break into pieces
decay.ex: The old apple on the ground is decaying.

fresh.ex: The bread is fresh and warm.

few.d: a small number of; not many
few.ex: There are only a few cookies left.

day.d: a time of 24 hours; also, the time when it is light

begin.ex: The class begins, and the teacher says hello.

soften.ex: The ice cream softens in the hot sun.

speck.ex: There is a speck of dirt on my white shirt.

appear.ex: A rainbow appeared after the rain.

cling.ex: The baby monkey clings to its mother.

pass.ex: The days pass quickly in summer.

eventually.d: in the end, after a long time
eventually.ex: We waited and waited. Eventually, the bus came.

covered.ex: The car is covered in snow.

earlier.ex: I got up earlier than my brother.

far.d: (before a word like "earlier" or "bigger") much; a lot
far.ex: My new bike is far faster than my old one.

just.ex: I just want one cookie, please.

suppose.d: to imagine; to think about what could happen
suppose.ex: Suppose you could fly. Where would you go?

mingle.d: to walk around and talk with different people
mingle.ex: At the party, Mom mingles with her friends.

outside.d: not in a building; out in the open air

humid.d: (about air) wet and often hot, so you feel sticky
humid.ex: It is humid today, and my shirt feels wet.

friend.d: a person you like and like to be with
friend.ex: My friends and I play ball after school.

sweat.d: water that comes out of your skin when you are hot
sweat.ex: After running, sweat drips down my face.

possibility.d: something that could happen or could be true
possibility.ex: There are many possibilities for the weekend: the zoo, the park or the beach.

endless.d: with no end; going on and on

examine.d: to look at something very carefully

make_connections.d: to see how what you read is like things you know
make_connections.ex: I make connections: the boy in the story has a dog like mine!

classroom.d: a room in a school where children learn

text_to_self.d: a connection between what you read and your own life
text_to_self.ex: Text to self: the girl in the book loves rain, and so do I!

under_microscope.d: when you look at it with a microscope
under_microscope.ex: Under a microscope, pond water is full of tiny living things.
